Sample: chicks with non-missing, non-zero net_rearing_manipulation (unmanipulated broods and 85 missing-manipulation chicks excluded), n=2720-> fitted n=2716 chicks in 319 rearing nests (1689 enlarged, 1027 reduced). Focal predictor: binary indicator enlarged = 1 if net_rearing_manipulation > 0, 0 if < 0. Native effect = -0.381 mm tarsus; SE 0.0447; Wald z = -8.52, p<0.001 (asymptotic z, no finite df). Observation unit = individual chick; design = randomized cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, clustered by rearing nest. Sex (29% missing) and post-treatment brood-size variables excluded.
rows.predictor: enlarged (1 = experimentally enlarged rearing brood, 0 = experimentally reduced)

rows.note: OLS on chick-level data (data.csv). Outcome: body-condition index = 100*day_14_weight/(day_14_tarsus_length^2). Predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing (post-manipulation rearing brood size = number of competing siblings+self). Season adjusted by continuous hatch_year trend + within-year-centred rear_nest_LD (no year dummies). Cluster-robust (rearing nest) SEs. Excluded rows with missing brood size or lay date; sex and post-treatment brood sizes not included. Native effect: -0.02834 index units per additional nestmate, SE 0.003799, Wald z = -7.46, df_resid = 3277, n = 3281 chicks in 393 rearing broods. Design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment; observation unit = chick at day 14.
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing (rearing brood size just after manipulation), continuous; higher = more sibling competition

rows.note: Design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation. Outcome: brood-mean day-14 chick mass (g) per rearing nest; WLS weighted by number of measured chicks in the nest, with hatch-year fixed effects (2001 baseline). Predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed chicks added to rearing nest; negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated). Excluded 85 chicks with '.' manipulation; sex (29% missing) and post-treatment brood-size variables not included. Dependence handled by aggregating to the rearing-nest level (unit of randomization) rather than clustered SEs. Native effect -0.1751 g per added chick, SE 0.0154, t = -11.37, df = 435, fitted n = 439 rearing nests (3635 chicks).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (net chicks added to the rearing nest, continuous, signed)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML) on day-14 mass (g): day_14_weight ~ rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing + C(hatch_year) + C(chick_sex_molec), random intercept for rearing nest (groups=rear_nest_breed_ID) plus a variance component for natal nest (hatch_nest_breed_ID). Sample: all chicks with non-missing post-manipulation rearing brood size, day-14 mass, year, both nest IDs, and molecular sex (n=2,385 chicks; 294 rearing-nest groups; observation unit = individual chick; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, 2001-2003). Focal predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing (continuous count of chicks in the rearing brood immediately after manipulation), coefficient = -0.1547 g per extra sibling, SE 0.0113, Wald z = -13.74 (large-sample normal, df not finite; n=2385). Unmanipulated broods retained since exposure is realized brood size, not treatment category.
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing (post-manipulation rearing brood size, chicks)

rows.note: OLS: size_pc1 ~ net_rearing_manipulation + C(hatch_year), cluster-robust SEs by rear_nest_breed_ID (439 clusters). Outcome = PC1 of standardized day-14 mass and tarsus length (equal +0.707 loadings, 79.6% variance, oriented higher = larger chick). n=3635 chicks (85 with '.' manipulation dropped); unmanipulated broods retained as 0. Sex and post-treatment brood-size variables excluded. Native scale: PC units per added chick; z = -11.21, df_resid = 3631. Unit = individual chick; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net number of chicks added to the rearing nest; negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated, positive = enlarged)

rows.note: OLS: day_14_weight (g) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + hatch-year dummies (2001 base), cluster-robust SEs on natal (hatch) nest. Sample: all 3,635 chicks with non-missing net_rearing_manipulation (85 chicks with "." dropped; unmanipulated broods retained at 0); reconstruction from rear_Cs_in - rear_Cs_out recovered none of the 85. Sex and post-treatment brood-size variables excluded. Native effect = grams of day-14 mass per one extra chick added to the rearing brood. z = -15.41, df_resid = 3631, 483 natal-nest clusters. Observation unit = chick; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, 2001-2003. Mixed-model alternative (random intercept for rearing nest) gave -0.181 (SE 0.016).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood; negative = reduced)

rows.note: OLS of day-14 mass (g) on binary enlarged indicator + hatch_year dummies + rear_nest_LD, rear_nest_CS, rear_nest_OH + molecular sex, SEs cluster-robust by rearing nest (249 clusters). Sample: chicks in matched manipulated rearing broods only (rear_nest_trt 5=enlarged, 6=reduced; unmanipulated trt 7 excluded because unmatched), dropping rows with '.' manipulation or missing sex/nest covariates. n=2076 chicks (observation unit = chick), df_resid=2068, z=-10.30. Native scale: grams per enlarged-vs-reduced contrast. Unadjusted/mixed-model variants gave -1.067 (SE 0.094) and -1.071 (SE 0.105).
rows.predictor: enlarged = 1 if rearing brood experimentally enlarged (trt 5), 0 if reduced (trt 6)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): day_14_tarsus_length (mm) ~ rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing + C(hatch_year), random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. Sample restricted to experimentally manipulated broods (net_rearing_manipulation non-missing and != 0), i.e. unmanipulated broods and 85 chicks with "." manipulation excluded. n = 2716 chicks (observation unit = chick) in 319 rearing nests; day-14 tarsus complete. Sex (29% missing) and post-treatment brood-size/fledging variables excluded. Focal effect = -0.0556 mm per extra sibling, SE 0.00650, Wald z = -8.54 (asymptotic, df = inf); year effects -0.154 (2002), -0.158 (2003); nest variance 0.117, residual scale 0.3125. Design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, clustered by rearing nest.
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing: post-manipulation rearing-brood size (number of nestmates incl. focal chick); larger = more sibling competition

rows.note: OLS: day_14_weight ~ rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing + C(hatch_year), SEs cluster-robust by rear_nest_breed_ID (399 clusters). n=3333 chicks (rows with missing rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing dropped; day-14 mass complete). Unit = individual chick; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment. Native scale grams per additional nestmate; z = -10.95, Wald test, df_resid = 3329. Sex and post-treatment day-14 brood size excluded (missingness / post-treatment).
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing: rearing-nest brood size immediately after manipulation (continuous, chicks)

rows.note: OLS: day_14_weight ~ rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing + C(hatch_year), cluster-robust SE by rear_nest_breed_ID (396 clusters). Excluded rows with '.' net_rearing_manipulation or missing brood/nest/year; unmanipulated broods retained (exposure is realized post-manipulation brood size, not treatment category). n=3315 chicks (observation unit = individual chick, day-14 measurement), cross-fostering brood-size manipulation design. Native scale: grams of day-14 mass per additional sibling. z=-10.98, cluster-robust Wald; df_resid=3311 (robust inference uses z). Mixed-model check with random rearing-nest intercept gave -0.141 (SE 0.0127).
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing: rearing-brood size immediately after manipulation (continuous count of nestmates)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): day_14_tarsus_length (mm) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + C(hatch_year), random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. Fitted n = 3635 chicks (85 chicks with '.' net_rearing_manipulation excluded by listwise deletion; reconstruction from rear_Cs_in - rear_Cs_out recovered none), 439 rearing nests; unmanipulated broods retained at net = 0. Observation unit = individual chick; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, exposure assigned at rearing-nest level. Native effect = mm of tarsus per extra chick added: -0.0662, SE 0.00767, Wald z = -8.64, p < 0.001, df = infinite (z-test); group variance 0.130, residual scale 0.296. Sex (29% missing) and post-treatment brood sizes excluded. Companion mass model gave -0.181 g/chick (SE 0.0158).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (positive = enlarged, negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated), continuous

rows.note: GEE (Gaussian identity, exchangeable within-cluster correlation, robust sandwich SEs) of day_14_weight (g) on a binary treatment contrast plus hatch-year fixed effects. Sample: cross-fostered chicks only (home_or_away==2) with non-missing net_rearing_manipulation and manipulation != 0, i.e. unmanipulated broods excluded; n=1329 chicks (834 enlarged, 495 reduced) clustered in 313 natal (hatch) nests; within-cluster correlation 0.62. Predictor: enlarged = 1 if net_rearing_manipulation > 0 (brood enlarged), 0 if < 0 (reduced). Estimate -1.043 g, SE 0.101, Wald z = -10.34 (df: large-sample z, no finite df). Observation unit = individual chick at day 14; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, 2001-2003. Excluded sex (29% missing) and post-treatment brood-size variables.
rows.predictor: enlarged (1 = experimentally enlarged rearing brood, 0 = reduced), from sign of net_rearing_manipulation

rows.note: Design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, exposure assigned at rearing-nest level. Complete-case chicks (non-'.' net_rearing_manipulation, molecular sex, home_or_away) aggregated to rearing-nest brood means of day-14 mass; WLS weighted by chicks per nest: mean_day14_weight ~ net_rearing_manipulation + C(hatch_year) + proportion female(sex==2). Native scale: grams of day-14 mass per additional chick added. Estimate -0.1698 g, SE 0.01705, t = -9.96, df = 312, fitted n = 317 rearing nests (2553 chicks); observation unit = rearing brood (nest mean). Post-treatment brood-size variables excluded to avoid conditioning on outcome of manipulation.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net number of chicks added to the rearing nest; negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated, positive = enlarged)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): y = 100*day_14_weight/day_14_tarsus_length^2 (body condition index, g/mm^2 x100) ~ enlarged + hatch_year fixed effects, random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. Sample: only experimentally manipulated chicks (net_rearing_manipulation non-missing and != 0), excluding unmanipulated broods and 85 chicks with '.' manipulation; n = 2,716 chicks (1,689 enlarged, 1,027 reduced) in 319 rearing nests. Focal contrast 'enlarged' = 1 if net_rearing_manipulation > 0, 0 if < 0. Native effect -0.2220, SE 0.0281, Wald z = -7.90, p < 1e-14, df = normal approximation (large-sample z). Observation unit: individual chick at day 14; design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, clustered by rearing nest. Sex excluded (29% missing); post-treatment brood-size variables excluded.
rows.predictor: enlarged (1 = experimentally enlarged rearing brood, 0 = experimentally reduced)

rows.note: Design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, Wytham Wood blue tits 2001-2003. Sample: chicks with non-missing net_rearing_manipulation and manipulation != 0 (unmanipulated broods and 85 chicks with '.' excluded), 2,716 chicks in 319 experimentally manipulated rearing nests. Analysis: nest-level aggregation (mean day-14 weight per rearing nest) then WLS weighted by number of chicks measured per nest, model y ~ net_rearing_manipulation + C(hatch_year); observation unit = rearing nest. Focal effect -0.1670 g per additional chick added, SE 0.01574, t(315) = -10.61, p < 1e-20. Native scale = grams of day-14 mass per chick added. Sex and post-treatment brood-size variables excluded (sex 29% missing; brood size post-treatment).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood; positive = enlarged, negative = reduced), nest-level value

rows.note: OLS: day_14_tarsus_length ~ enlarged + C(hatch_year), fitted to the 2,716 chicks in experimentally manipulated rearing broods (net_rearing_manipulation != 0; 85 chicks with missing manipulation excluded by listwise deletion, unmanipulated broods excluded). Focal predictor: binary indicator enlarged = 1 if net_rearing_manipulation > 0 (enlarged rearing brood), 0 if < 0 (reduced). SEs cluster-robust on hatch (natal) nest ID (483 nests overall; 363 clusters in this sample). Native effect = -0.3700 mm, SE 0.0329, Wald z = -11.23, df_resid = 2712 (cluster-robust z inference), n = 2716 chicks (observation unit = individual chick), design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, 2001-2003. Covariates: year fixed effects only; sex omitted (29% missing); post-treatment brood sizes omitted. Companion fit on mass gave -0.175 g per added chick (SE 0.0114).
rows.predictor: enlarged brood indicator (1 = experimentally enlarged rearing brood, 0 = reduced)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): log(day_14_tarsus_length) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + C(hatch_year), random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. Sample: all chicks with non-missing net_rearing_manipulation (85 chicks with "." excluded after checking they could not be reconstructed from rear_Cs_in - rear_Cs_out); unmanipulated broods retained at net=0. n = 3,635 chicks (observation unit = individual chick at day 14) in 439 rearing nests; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, 2001-2003. Focal effect: -0.004032 log-mm per added chick (SE 0.000464), i.e. ~-0.40% tarsus per extra chick; Wald t = -8.68, df ≈ 435 (nests - 4 fixed params), p ≈ 8e-17. No sex covariate (29% missing) and no post-treatment brood-size variables included. Companion fits: day-14 mass -0.181 g/chick (SE 0.0158); raw tarsus -0.0662 mm/chick (SE 0.0077).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to the rearing nest (positive = enlarged, negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated)

rows.note: GEE (Gaussian, identity link, exchangeable working correlation within rearing nest, robust sandwich SEs; ICC=0.487) of day-14 body-condition index (day_14_weight/day_14_tarsus_length^2 ×100, g/mm^2×100) on a binary experimental contrast enlarged(1) vs reduced(0), plus hatch-year fixed effects (2001 reference). Exclusions: 85 chicks with '.' net_rearing_manipulation; unmanipulated broods (net=0) excluded so the contrast is purely experimental. n=2716 chicks (obs unit = individual chick at day 14) in 319 rearing nests (clusters). Native effect −0.2222 index units, SE 0.0276, Wald z = −8.05, p<1e-14 (GEE: z-based, no finite residual df). Design: randomized-ish cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, chicks nested in rearing nests. Year effects: 2002 +0.111, 2003 +0.028.
rows.predictor: enlarged = 1 if net_rearing_manipulation > 0, 0 if < 0 (experimentally enlarged vs reduced rearing brood)

rows.note: Brood-level WLS. Outcome: rearing-nest mean of chick day-14 body-condition index 100*day_14_weight/day_14_tarsus_length^2. Exposure: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing (post-manipulation rearing brood size = number of competing siblings+self). Covariates: within-year-centred rearing-nest lay date and continuous year trend (no year dummies). Aggregated to 393 rearing nests (from 3281 chicks with non-missing brood size, lay date, mass, tarsus), weighted by chicks measured per nest. Native effect -0.02803 condition-index units per additional sibling, SE 0.00394, t = -7.112, df = 389. Observation unit: rearing brood (chick-level data aggregated); design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, observational contrast in realized brood size. Excluded: chicks with missing brood size or lay date; sex not used (29% missing); post-treatment day-14 brood size and fledging counts not used.
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing (post-manipulation rearing brood size, chicks; higher = more sibling competition)
